    - Juna, then her daughter Hazel, then Hazel's son Corin, then me. My parents died of a winter fever when I was three, so Grandmother Hazel raised me, in a crooked house round the back of the Old Barracks. She sewed for a living.
    - She lived to eighty-eight and never once introduced me as a Marrow. Everybody else does. I miss her.
    - Everybody expects me to write one as good as Juna's. So I have written three and burned two, which is a very Marrow thing to do, apparently. Dina has been my teacher since I was small. She has never asked to read them. That is how I know she wants to.
